scene.picture: One continuous flat-vector space scene on a deep violet-navy vertical gradient with a soft purple haze in the middle, about 170 small star dots (violet and pale lavender, 1 to 4 px, some breathing in opacity) and about 14 four-point sparkles. A tiny Earth (blue disc with green land blotches) sits near the top at x 540, y 390; a dotted violet measuring line runs straight down to a tiny Moon at y 1360, each with a rounded colour tag to the right ("Earth" blue, a long distance tag violet). From 0.45 s the bodies slide in one at a time every 0.29 s from alternate sides (left, right) with a rotation that unwinds and a small overshoot, stacking to scale in a column on the line: three tiny rocky bodies share one grey tag on the left, then a huge banded orange-cream body, a banded cream body with a tilted ring, a cyan body and a blue body; each body is a flat disc with darker bands or blotches clipped inside, a large dark night-side ellipse over its left part leaving a lit crescent on the right, a faint soft highlight top-right and a blurred halo of its own colour. Each body gets a pill tag in its own saturated hue that pops in (scale 0 to 1 with overshoot) 0.2 s after it lands. At 2.53 s (payoff) the last body lands, the scene pulses (scale 1.035 then settles), the measuring line turns mint green, a mint bracket marks the spare gap with a mint tag holding a number with its unit, and a hot-pink chip with a yellow check disc pops in at the top, tilted -3 degrees. One white caption line (about 46 px, medium weight, sentence case, soft dark shadow) sits low at y about 1435 and swaps in place three times: question part 1, question part 2, answer.

review_story.summary: A 4-second flat-vector space shot that asks a yes/no scale question in two caption parts and answers it by stacking objects to scale on a measured line.
review_story.hook: 0 to 1.3 s: a near-empty star field with one tiny object at the top and a dotted line to a second tiny object far below, while the caption asks the first half of a surprising question; the empty gap i
highlights: 0.45 to 2.5 s: objects slide in one at a time, alternating sides, each landing in the gap with an overshoot and its own colour tag: a steady rhythm that makes the viewer count along.

2.53 s: the payoff lands on a visual hit: the scene pulses, the line turns green, a bracket shows the leftover room with its real number, and a pink check chip stamps the answer: the answer is seen, n
Everything is drawn to scale on one measured line, so the comparison is honest and instantly readable (tiny things share one tag, big ones get their own).
